text: Which HTML5 element is the most appropriate semantic tag to wrap the main navigation links of a website?

options.A: <nav>
options.B: <section>
options.C: <ul>
options.D: <menu>

explanation: The HTML5 <nav> element is specifically designed to contain blocks of major navigation links.

text: Why should you use semantic HTML5 elements instead of generic <div> tags?

options.A: They improve accessibility for screen readers and aid search engine optimization (SEO)
options.B: They automatically apply CSS styling to the wrapped content
options.C: They prevent JavaScript script errors from crashing the page load
options.D: They compress the HTML file size to load pages faster

explanation: Semantic tags give meaning to the structure of the document, making it easier for search engines to index and assistive tech to read.

text: Which semantic element is used to represent independent, self-contained content that could be distributed in an RSS feed (e.g. blog post, forum post)?

options.A: <article>
options.B: <section>
options.C: <aside>
options.D: <main>

explanation: <article> is intended for self-contained blocks that make sense independently, whereas <section> is for thematic grouping of content.

text: What is the correct way to link an image with an alternative text description for accessibility?
explanation: The 'alt' attribute provides alternative text that screen readers read and is displayed if the image fails to load.

text: What does the HTML5 <aside> element represent?

options.A: Content tangentially related to the content around it, like a sidebar or pull quotes
options.B: A dialog modal box that pops up on the side of the screen
options.C: A section that contains navigation links only
options.D: The footer area at the very bottom of the webpage

explanation: <aside> wraps secondary content related to main topics, frequently rendered as sidebars, advertising blocks, or callouts.

text: In CSS Flexbox, which property controls the alignment of items along the main axis?

options.A: justify-content
options.B: align-items
options.C: flex-direction
options.D: align-content

explanation: justify-content aligns flex items horizontally (or vertically if flex-direction is column) along the main axis. align-items handles the cross axis.

text: What does 'align-items: center' do in a flex container?

options.A: Centers the flex items along the cross axis
options.B: Centers the flex items along the main axis
options.C: Forces the flex items to wrap onto a new row
options.D: Arranges the flex items in a grid layout layout

explanation: align-items specifies default alignment for items along the cross axis (e.g. vertical centering in a default row layout).

text: What is the key difference between CSS Grid and CSS Flexbox?

options.A: Grid is two-dimensional (rows and columns); Flexbox is one-dimensional (row or column)
options.B: Flexbox is only for mobile layouts; Grid is strictly for desktop layouts
options.C: Grid requires JavaScript to render; Flexbox does not
options.D: Flexbox does not support aligning items vertically

explanation: Grid is designed for two-dimensional layouts, letting you place items in rows and columns. Flexbox is designed for linear layouts in one direction.

text: Which CSS Grid property defines the sizes of the columns in a grid layout?

options.A: grid-template-columns
options.B: grid-column-gap
options.C: grid-auto-flow
options.D: grid-template-areas

explanation: grid-template-columns specifies the number of columns and their widths (e.g. using px, %, or the fr unit) in a grid.

text: What does the CSS grid unit 'fr' represent?

options.A: A fraction of the free space available in the grid container
options.B: A fixed relative font size based on the root element
options.C: A metric equivalent to 10 pixels of screen width
options.D: The frame refresh rate of the browser window

explanation: The 'fr' unit is a fractional unit. grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr divides space so the second column is twice as wide as the first.

text: What is a main characteristic of JavaScript arrow functions compared to traditional functions?

options.A: They do not have their own 'this' binding; they inherit 'this' lexically from parent scope
options.B: They cannot accept arguments or parameters
options.C: They are compiled instead of interpreted by browser engines
options.D: They cannot be used as callback handlers in event listeners

explanation: Arrow functions do not bind their own 'this'. Instead, they capture the 'this' value of the enclosing context.

text: Which state transition represents a JavaScript Promise that completed successfully?

options.A: fulfilled
options.B: pending
options.C: rejected
options.D: resolved_fail

explanation: A Promise has three states: pending (in progress), fulfilled (success, resolved), and rejected (error, failed).

text: How do you handle error rejections when using async/await syntax in JavaScript?

options.A: Wrap the await statements in a try...catch block
options.B: Append a .catch() method to the async function declaration
options.C: Use the error-first callback pattern in function arguments
options.D: JavaScript handles all async errors silently without crashing

explanation: async/await acts synchronously. Wrapping await calls inside a try...catch block catches Promise rejections as standard exceptions.

text: What is 'destructuring assignment' in ES6?

options.A: Unpacking values from arrays or properties from objects into distinct variables
options.B: Deleting unused objects from memory to prevent memory leaks
options.C: Splitting a single code file into multiple modular scripts
options.D: Converting a JSON string back into a JavaScript object

explanation: Destructuring is a syntax (e.g. const { name } = user) that extracts properties from objects or arrays concisely.

text: What does the JavaScript 'spread operator' (...) do when applied to an array?

options.A: Expands the elements of the array into individual arguments or elements
options.B: Sums up all the numeric values in the array
options.C: Sorts the array in alphabetical order
options.D: Converts the array elements into lowercase strings

explanation: The spread operator expands an iterable array into separate values, allowing quick array copying or joining (e.g. [...arr1, ...arr2]).

text: What hook is used to perform side effects (like data fetching, subscriptions) in React functional components?

options.A: useEffect
options.B: useState
options.C: useContext
options.D: useReducer

explanation: useEffect lets functional components interact with external APIs or perform actions when state/props change.

text: Why should you never modify a React state variable directly (e.g. state.value = 5)?

options.A: React will not detect the change, and the component will not re-render
options.B: It throws a compiler syntax error during build
options.C: It permanently deletes the state variable from local memory
options.D: It causes other components to lose their props data

explanation: React state must be updated using the provided setter function (e.g. setState) so React can track changes and trigger re-renders.

text: What is the purpose of the React hook 'useMemo'?

options.A: To cache and return the memoized result of an expensive calculation
options.B: To store values that persist across browser tab restarts
options.C: To create reference links to physical HTML DOM nodes
options.D: To fetch data from backend REST APIs asynchronously

explanation: useMemo caches (memoizes) the return value of a computation, recalculating it only when its input dependencies change.

text: How does 'useCallback' differ from 'useMemo' in React?

options.A: useCallback caches a function instance itself; useMemo caches the result of calling a function
options.B: useCallback only works in class components; useMemo is for functional components
options.C: useCallback is used for API calls; useMemo is for styling
options.D: There is no difference; they are interchangeable aliases

explanation: useCallback(fn, deps) is equivalent to useMemo(() => fn, deps). It prevents child components from re-rendering due to recreated callback functions.

text: What is the purpose of the 'key' prop in React when rendering a list of elements?

options.A: To help React identify which items have changed, been added, or been removed
options.B: To encrypt the rendered list elements for secure display
options.C: To apply unique CSS class styling to list rows
options.D: To link the list elements to database primary key values

explanation: Keys provide identity to array elements, helping React's reconciliation algorithm update the DOM efficiently without rebuilding the list.

text: Which HTTP method should be used to update an existing resource partially in a REST API?

options.A: PATCH
options.B: PUT
options.C: POST
options.D: GET

explanation: PATCH modifies an existing resource partially. PUT replaces the entire resource. POST creates a new resource.

text: What does a '403 Forbidden' HTTP status code represent?

options.A: The client is authenticated, but does not have permission to access the resource
options.B: The client lacks valid authentication credentials (not logged in)
options.C: The requested API endpoint does not exist on the server
options.D: The server encountered an unexpected error processing the request

explanation: 401 represents Unauthorized (not logged in). 403 represents Forbidden (authenticated, but lacking permission/scope).

text: What design constraint states that a REST API request must contain all context needed to process it, without depending on server-side session state?

options.A: Statelessness
options.B: Client-Server
options.C: Cacheability
options.D: Uniform Interface

explanation: Statelessness requires each request to be self-contained (e.g. including authorization headers), making scaling easier since servers don't store session state.

text: What Node.js module is used to import code or packages in CommonJS format?

options.A: require()
options.B: import
options.C: fetch()
options.D: include()

explanation: CommonJS uses const module = require('module_name') to load files and packages in Node.js. ES Modules use 'import'.

text: In Express, what is 'middleware'?

options.A: Functions that have access to the request, response, and next middleware function in the cycle
options.B: The database storage layer between SQL and the server
options.C: Styling scripts running inside the user's browser window
options.D: Compiler tools that translate JS files to binary machine code

explanation: Middleware are pipeline functions (e.g. body-parsers, auth checkers) that run sequentially, modifying request/response or ending the cycle.

text: What is the purpose of call next() inside an Express middleware function?

options.A: To pass control of the request to the next middleware function in the stack
options.B: To send the final JSON response payload back to the client
options.C: To terminate the active Node.js server process safely
options.D: To redirect the user's browser to the dashboard page

explanation: If a middleware doesn't send a response, it must call next() to pass execution forward, otherwise the request hangs.

text: Which database type is characterized by structured tables, predefined schemas, and SQL query interfaces?

options.A: Relational Database (RDBMS)
options.B: NoSQL Database
options.C: Key-Value Store
options.D: Graph Database

explanation: Relational databases (like PostgreSQL, MySQL) store data in tabular rows/columns, enforcing strict relationship schemas.

text: What type of NoSQL database is MongoDB?

options.A: Document database
options.B: Key-value store
options.C: Wide-column store
options.D: Graph database

explanation: MongoDB stores data as BSON documents (similar to JSON), which is the document database model.

text: What is the benefit of database normalisation?

options.A: It reduces data redundancy and improves data integrity
options.B: It increases the query execution speed of JOIN statements
options.C: It encrypts table columns to protect passwords
options.D: It automatically generates database backup files

explanation: Normalization organizes columns and tables to ensure dependencies are logical, reducing redundancy and minimizing data anomalies.

text: What is a JSON Web Token (JWT) composed of?

options.A: Header, Payload, Signature
options.B: Username, Password, Salt
options.C: Access Token, Refresh Token, Secret
options.D: IP Address, Timestamp, Session ID

explanation: A JWT is a string of three Base64URL-encoded parts separated by dots: Header (meta/alg), Payload (claims), and Signature (verification).

text: Why should JWTs be stored in HttpOnly cookies instead of LocalStorage?

options.A: To protect them from access via client-side JavaScript, preventing XSS-based theft
options.B: To increase the expiration time of the token automatically
options.C: To allow the browser to edit the token values dynamically
options.D: To bypass the need for SSL/TLS encryption on request payloads

explanation: LocalStorage is readable by JavaScript. If an attacker runs malicious JS (XSS), they can steal the tokens. HttpOnly cookies cannot be read by JS.

text: What is OAuth 2.0?

options.A: An authorization framework enabling applications to obtain limited access to user accounts on an HTTP service
options.B: A hashing library used to encrypt user passwords in database tables
options.C: An encryption protocol that secures Wi-Fi network routers
options.D: A database synchronization tool used across cloud providers

explanation: OAuth 2.0 is an authorization protocol (not authentication) that allows users to grant apps access to their resources without sharing passwords.

text: What type of attack involves an attacker injecting malicious scripts into trusted websites, which then run in user browsers?

options.A: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
options.B: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
options.C: SQL Injection
options.D: Man-in-the-Middle

explanation: XSS occurs when an app includes untrusted data in a webpage without validation, causing the browser to execute injected scripts.

text: What security vulnerability involves executing arbitrary database queries by entering malicious inputs in input fields?

options.A: SQL Injection
options.B: Cross-Site Scripting
options.C: CSRF
options.D: Distributed Denial of Service

explanation: SQLi occurs when input is concatenated directly into SQL queries without parametrization or escaping, executing malicious commands.

text: What security header is used to specify which dynamic resources are allowed to load and execute on a webpage?

options.A: Content-Security-Policy (CSP)
options.B: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy
options.C: Strict-Transport-Security
options.D: X-Frame-Options

explanation: CSP is an HTTP response header that restricts where resources (scripts, styles, images) can be fetched and loaded from, preventing XSS.

text: What is the primary way to prevent SQL Injection in backend servers?

options.A: Using parameterized queries (prepared statements)
options.B: Encrypting the entire SQL database on the server
options.C: Limiting input fields to a maximum of 10 characters
options.D: Changing database passwords every month

explanation: Parameterized queries separate the query code from the user input variables, ensuring input is treated strictly as data, not command code.

text: What is the purpose of 'CSRF tokens' in web security?

options.A: To verify that a request is originating from the authentic, authorized user interface of the app
options.B: To encrypt the access token cookie value
options.C: To keep the user's login session active for longer durations
options.D: To scan incoming uploads for potential malware

explanation: CSRF tokens are unique secrets generated by the server for a user session. Forms must submit this token, blocking unauthorized cross-site requests.

text: In responsive design, what is a 'media query' used for?

options.A: Applying different CSS styles based on the device's screen size or screen attributes
options.B: Querying the database for image and video files
options.C: Checking if the browser supports JavaScript async functions
options.D: Configuring the default layout width of the webpage container

explanation: Media queries (@media) allow styles to scale dynamically, adapting layouts for mobile phones, tablets, and desktop screens.

text: What HTML meta tag is essential to ensure responsive scaling on mobile device screens?

options.A: <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0'>
options.B: <meta name='responsive' content='true'>
options.C: <meta name='scale' content='mobile-first'>
options.D: <meta name='device' content='auto'>

explanation: The viewport meta tag instructs mobile browsers to render the page layout width matching the physical device screen width, preventing layout shrinking.

text: What does a 'mobile-first' CSS development strategy imply?

options.A: Writing base CSS rules for mobile screens first, then adding media queries for larger screens
options.B: Restricting the web application to run exclusively on smartphones
options.C: Excluding all image files from the CSS layouts to speed up mobile page load
options.D: Designing mobile applications in native Java/Swift before writing HTML code

explanation: Mobile-first CSS writes default styles for small screens, using min-width media queries to overlay styles as screens widen.
